# Banned emitter strings (ADR 0437, Gap R.288).
#
# One phrase per line; `#` starts a comment. This list is asked of the strings the COMPILER emits —
# the string literals in `pkg/lang/*.go` and `cmd/gustyc/*.go` that a user or an agent reads out of a
# diagnostic — while witness-banned-phrases.txt is asked of the files that make claims (the tests, the
# CLI, the case registry, the agent-facing documents). The two lists are read together: an offer to run
# a program the way this toolchain retired is as false in a message as it is in a document, and the
# reader who follows it is the same reader either way.
#
# What is specific to a message is the SHAPE of the offer. A document can name the retired engine in
# prose about the retirement; a refusal cannot tell the reader to go and run the program that way,
# because since ADR 0302 there is one way to run a program here and `--interp` is a usage error.
#
# A literal that carries a marker from witness-history-markers.txt is licensed — a diagnostic that
# says "the engine that was retired" is telling the reader what happened, not offering a way to run.
#
# the second way to run, offered
run it interpreted
run it in the interpreter
run it through the interpreter
run it on the interpreter
run the program interpreted
run the program in the interpreter
run this program interpreted
run your program interpreted
run it aot or interpreted
or run it\b
#
# the retired flag, offered as a way to run
--interp\b
#
# the retired entry points, offered as a callable way to run
EvalExpr
EvalProgram
InterpreterRun
